capability: A harness map that shows only real links
title: Draw only the joins you see.

hook.picture: Close on the whale presenting a tidy map of boxes joined by neat lines. A pod follows one line into a box and finds it empty: a copper ✕.
hook.words: The map said it was all wired.

problem_in_viewer_words.body: Our diagram showed it all connected. Half of it was never built.
problem_in_viewer_words.who: engineering director before a board review

why_it_keeps_happening.picture: Pull back: three tidy maps side by side. On the first, someone adds a hopeful line and a pod falls through (2 beats). It repeats, faster each time.
why_it_keeps_happening.words: Hopeful lines look the same as real ones.

stakes.body: Leaders fund, promise and staff against a picture of a system that does not exist yet.

solution_hint: Draw what the source shows. Mark the gaps.

metaphor.body: The map keeps only the joins found in the source, drawn teal. Planned but unbuilt joins stay on the map in copper, and the pinned base of rules has no false lines drawn out of it.

steps.picture: Lines redraw: only the joins found in the source stay, in teal. A pinned stone at the bottom of the map holds the rules.
steps.words: Keep only joins the source shows.

steps.picture: Six planned joins that are not built turn copper. They stay on the map, plainly marked, not hidden.
steps.words: Not built yet? Show it in copper.

steps.picture: Push-in on the pinned base: no lines go out of it. The whale reaches to draw one so it looks connected. The pen stops.
Teal joins get a small check tick; copper joins get a named tag.
steps.words: Checked joins are seams. Copper ones are gaps.
steps.sound: Woodblock and knock, in tune together

real_case.claim: Harness review: edges only where the source shows them; six first-class facts drawn terracotta as named unbuilt items; the kernel has no outgoing package edges.

honest_limit.picture: A pod runs through a teal join, so the wiring is real, but it comes out with a copper smudge. The map stays teal.
honest_limit.words: Wired does not mean it works.

not_this.body: An honest map is not a test.

ending_pattern.body: The same presentation as act 1, but the map now shows its gaps in copper, so the audience sees what is real before anyone falls through.
ending_pattern.callback: Act 1's neat line into an empty box is now a copper gap the pod stops at.

end_belief.body: Show the gaps. Never draw hopeful lines.

score_self.reason: The felt pain (a diagram that lies) is universal for leaders. The real case comes from Manu's own review, and the limit (wired is not working) is honest and visible. The callback is exact.
